m: Toast coarsely cracked pepper in a dry pan 1 min until fragrant.
Boil pasta in lightly salted water; the cheese is salty. Reserve 1 cup starchy water.
Off heat, whisk pecorino with a splash of warm (not boiling) pasta water into a thick paste.
Toss pasta with pepper and paste, adding pasta water until glossy and creamy.
p: The sauce breaks above ~65°C: work off the heat and the starch does the emulsifying for you.

i: 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery rib, fine dice
m: Render pancetta; sweat the soffritto 10 min until soft, not browned.
Brown the meats hard, breaking them up; stir in tomato paste and cook 2 min.
Deglaze with wine, add milk and stock; simmer partly covered 2–3 hours, topping up with stock.
Toss with tagliatelle and a splash of pasta water; finish with Parmigiano.
p: Milk isn't optional: its proteins keep the meat tender and mellow the acidity.

m: Mix dough, rest 20 min, knead briefly until smooth; cold-ferment 24–72 h for flavor (or 2 h warm).
Divide into 4 balls; proof 2 h at room temp. Preheat a steel or stone at max heat 45 min.
Stretch from the center out, keeping a rim. Top sparingly: tomato, mozzarella, oil.
Bake 6–8 min until leopard-spotted; finish with basil.
p: Wet, sparse toppings are why home pizza goes soggy: less is structural, not aesthetic.

m: Sweat onion in half the butter; toast rice 2 min until edges turn translucent.
Deglaze with wine. Add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, ~18 min.
Bloom saffron in a ladle of stock and add halfway through.
Off heat, beat in cold butter and Parmigiano (the mantecatura) until it flows like lava.
p: Stir for creaminess, but stop at al dente: it keeps cooking on the plate.

i: 2 chicken breasts, halved and pounded thin
m: Season and flour the cutlets; sear 2–3 min per side in oil + 1 tbsp butter; remove.
Deglaze with wine, scraping the fond; reduce by half.
Add lemon juice and capers; swirl in remaining butter off heat.
Return chicken to coat; shower with parsley.
p: The flour dredge isn't just for browning; it thickens the pan sauce.

i: Rosemary, Parmigiano rind if you have it
m: Sweat vegetables in olive oil; add garlic, rosemary, tomato paste.
Add beans, stock, and the cheese rind; simmer 20 min.
Blend a third of the soup for body; return and cook pasta directly in it.
Finish with good oil and grated cheese.
p: Cooking the pasta in the soup releases starch that turns broth into velvet.

m: Salt eggplant 30 min; pat dry. Fry or roast at 220°C until deeply golden.
Simmer a quick garlic-basil tomato sauce, 15 min.
Layer sauce, eggplant, both cheeses; repeat, ending with Parmigiano.
Bake 190°C for 30 min; rest 15 min before cutting.
p: Resting is the difference between clean layers and a delicious landslide.

m: Whisk yolks and sugar over a bain-marie until pale and thick; cool.
Fold in mascarpone until just smooth: don't overbeat.
Dip biscuits in espresso for one second per side; layer with cream twice.
Chill 6+ hours; dust cocoa just before serving.
p: A one-second dip. The biscuits finish softening in the fridge.

i: 50ml olive oil plus more for the pan
m: Mix to a wet, shaggy dough; four sets of folds over 2 hours (or overnight cold).
Pour into an oiled pan; let relax and rise 1 hour until bubbly.
Oil your fingers and dimple firmly to the bottom; top with rosemary and salt.
Bake 220°C, 22–25 min, until deep gold.
p: The dimples aren't decoration: they trap oil and stop giant tunnels forming.

m: Sear shrimp 1 min per side in olive oil; remove before fully cooked.
Soften garlic and chili gently; deglaze with wine and reduce.
Mount with butter, add lemon; return shrimp 1 min to finish.
Toss with linguine and parsley.
p: Shrimp overcook in the time it takes to find your tongs: pull them early, always.

m: Beat eggs completely smooth with salt; no streaks of white.
Melt butter over medium in a nonstick pan until foaming, not brown.
Add eggs; stir rapidly with a fork or spatula while shaking the pan until softly set curds form.
Off heat, let the base set 10 seconds, then roll onto the plate seam-side down.
p: Pale gold outside, custard inside. Browning is a flavor choice: in Paris, it's a mistake.

m: Render lardons; brown chicken hard in the fat; set both aside.
Brown onions and mushrooms; add garlic and flour, cook 2 min.
Deglaze with wine, add stock and herbs; return chicken, simmer 45–60 min.
Reduce the sauce until it coats a spoon; finish with a knob of butter.
p: Reduce the wine by half before adding stock if you want a deeper, less boozy sauce.

m: Cook onions in butter over medium-low with a pinch of salt 45–60 min to deep mahogany.
Stir in flour; deglaze with wine, add stock and thyme; simmer 20 min.
Ladle into ovenproof bowls; top with toasted baguette and a blanket of Gruyère.
Broil until molten and bronzed.
p: If the onions catch, deglaze with a splash of water and keep going: those dark patches are the soup.

m: Cut everything to equal 2cm dice.
Sauté each vegetable separately until browned; this is the whole secret.
Combine with tomatoes, garlic, herbs; simmer gently 20 min.
Rest: it's better warm or next day, with torn basil.
p: Crowded vegetables steam. Separate batches taste like Provence; one batch tastes like cafeteria.

m: Dry the fish obsessively; season and dredge in flour, shaking off excess.
Sear in half the butter 2 min per side until golden; plate.
Add remaining butter; cook to beurre noisette, nutty and hazelnut-brown.
Add lemon juice off heat (it will spit), pour over fish, add parsley.
p: Watch the milk solids: foam, then quiet, then brown. Quiet is your 10-second warning.

m: Brown beef in batches until crusted; render lardons.
Sauté aromatics, add flour and paste; deglaze with wine.
Add stock and herbs; braise covered at 160°C for 2.5–3 h until fork-tender.
Sauté mushrooms and onions separately; fold in and reduce sauce to gloss.
p: Batches, always. Gray meat makes gray stew.

i: 1 blind-baked tart shell (200g flour, 100g butter, pinch salt, cold water)
m: Blind-bake the shell fully: pale pastry never recovers.
Render lardons; scatter in the shell with cheese if using.
Whisk custard; season with nutmeg. Pour into shell on the oven rack.
Bake 160°C ~30 min until it barely trembles at the center.
p: A quiche is a custard in a crust. Treat it like crème brûlée, not a frittata.

i: Pinch salt, 1 tbsp sugar for sweet
m: Blend everything smooth; rest 30 min so the flour hydrates.
Heat a lightly buttered pan; pour a thin layer, swirling immediately.
Flip when the edges lace and lift, ~1 min; 20 seconds more.
Stack under a towel; fill with lemon-sugar, jam, or ham and Gruyère.
p: The first crêpe belongs to the cook. Every French grandmother agrees.

m: Warm cream with vanilla. Whisk yolks and sugar; temper in the cream.
Strain into ramekins; bake in a water bath at 150°C, 30–35 min, until just wobbly.
Chill 4+ hours.
Sprinkle a thin, even layer of sugar; torch to amber glass.
p: Two thin torched layers beat one thick one: better crack, no burnt patches.

i: Dijon vinaigrette: 1 tbsp mustard, 2 tbsp vinegar, 6 tbsp olive oil
m: Boil potatoes; blanch beans until snappy and shock in ice water.
Whisk the vinaigrette; season assertively.
Dress potatoes while warm: they drink it in.
Compose everything on a platter; never toss into confetti.
p: Warm potatoes + vinaigrette is a technique you'll reuse for every potato salad forever.

m: Steep kombu in barely-simmering water 10 min; remove before it boils.
Add katsuobushi, cut heat, steep 3 min; strain. This is dashi.
Warm dashi with tofu and rehydrated wakame.
Dissolve miso through a strainer off the boil; add scallions.
p: Boiled miso goes flat and gritty. It's a finishing seasoning, not an ingredient to cook.

m: Crisp the thighs skin-down over medium, pressing, 8 min; flip 3 min. Drain fat.
Add the mixed sauce; simmer and turn to glaze, 2–3 min, until syrupy.
Rest, slice, spoon over the glaze; serve with rice.
p: Real teriyaki is a pan glaze, not a marinade: the sauce reduces onto crisp skin.

i: 2 cups short-grain rice, cooked and warm
m: Wet your hands, salt your palms.
Take a handful of warm rice, tuck a spoon of filling in the center.
Press into a triangle with firm, gentle turns: 3 presses, rotate, repeat.
Wrap with nori just before eating so it stays crisp.
p: Compress just enough to hold. An onigiri should fall apart in the mouth, not in the hand.

i: Curry roux blocks (or make roux + curry powder + garam masala)
Secret weapons: grated apple, splash soy
m: Brown the meat; sweat onions until golden.
Add vegetables and water; simmer 15 min.
Off heat, dissolve roux fully; return to a gentle simmer to thicken.
Add apple and soy; serve over rice with pickles.
p: Roux clumps in boiling liquid; kill the heat first, then melt it in.

i: Dip: soy + rice vinegar + chili oil
m: Squeeze the salted cabbage dry; mix with pork and aromatics until sticky.
Fill, wet the edge, pleat one side against the flat side.
Fry flat-side down until golden; add 60ml water, cover, steam 3 min.
Uncover, crisp the bottoms again; serve dark side up.
p: Fry–steam–fry is the whole game. The water finishes the filling; the second fry restores the crunch.

i: 2 tbsp each soy and mirin, 1 tsp sugar
m: Simmer onion in the seasoned dashi until soft; add chicken, cook through.
Pour egg in two stages: first two-thirds, swirl gently, cover 1 min.
Add the rest; kill heat while still runny.
Slide over hot rice: the egg finishes on the way to the table.
p: The eggs should be three textures at once: set, soft, and raw. Aim for underdone.

i: Sauce: 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 1 tbsp each oyster sauce, ketchup, soy
m: Sear pork hard; add vegetables, stir-fry 2 min.
Add loosened noodles with a splash of water; toss.
Pour sauce around the edge of the pan so it sizzles and caramelizes.
Top with aonori and beni shoga.
p: Sauce hitting hot steel, not noodles, is where the street-stall flavor comes from.

i: 2 tbsp dashi (kombu dashi keeps it vegetarian)
m: Whisk everything; strain for silkiness.
Oil a pan (rectangular ideal); pour a thin layer, roll it to one end when barely set.
Oil again, pour more egg, lifting the roll so it flows underneath; roll again.
Repeat until used up; shape in a sushi mat if you have one, slice.
p: Each layer glues to the last while still wet: patience loses, momentum wins.

i: Tare per bowl: 1.5 tbsp soy, 1 tsp mirin, ½ tsp sesame oil
m: Steep kombu in stock 20 min at a bare simmer; season lightly.
Mix tare in each bowl: the bowl seasons the soup, not the pot.
Cook noodles separately; never in the broth.
Assemble: tare, broth, noodles, toppings. Serve screaming hot.
p: Ramen is assembly, not soup-making: broth, tare, noodles, and toppings are four separate projects.

i: 2 sushi-grade salmon fillets or hot-seared salmon
Warm sushi rice (rice + 2 tbsp seasoned vinegar)
m: Season warm rice with sushi vinegar; fan to glossy.
Slice salmon against the grain (raw) or sear 2 min a side and flake.
Bowl the rice; arrange salmon, avocado, cucumber.
Finish with sesame, nori, and sauce.
p: Body-temperature rice, cool fish: the temperature contrast is the luxury.

m: Break the cold rice apart with wet hands.
Scramble eggs in hot oil until barely set; remove.
Blast rice over the highest heat, pressing and tossing until it dances and smells toasty.
Return eggs, add soy around the rim, scallions, sesame oil. Done in 90 seconds.
p: Day-old rice isn't tradition, it's chemistry: retrograded starch fries instead of steams.

i: 450g soft tofu, cubed and steeped in hot salted water
m: Fry pork crisp; add doubanjiang and beans, fry until the oil turns red.
Add aromatics, then stock; slide in tofu, simmer 5 min without stirring hard.
Thicken with slurry in two additions.
Finish with ground Sichuan peppercorn and scallion.
p: Steeping the tofu in hot brine firms and seasons it so it survives the wok.

i: 800g pork shoulder, cut into long strips
3 tbsp hoisin, 2 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp honey
Red fermented tofu (optional, for the classic hue)
m: Marinate pork 4–24 hours; reserve marinade.
Roast at 200°C on a rack, 30–40 min, turning once.
Boil the marinade with extra honey into a glaze; brush every 10 min.
Finish under the broiler for charred, lacquered edges. Rest, slice thick.
p: Shoulder over tenderloin: you want fat cap and char, not lean and dry.

i: 500g chicken thigh, diced, velveted (1 tsp each soy, wine, cornstarch)
Sauce: 1 tbsp each soy, black vinegar, sugar; 1 tsp dark soy; slurry
m: Sizzle chilies and peppercorns in oil until fragrant, not black.
Add chicken; stir-fry until golden at the edges.
Add scallions, then the sauce; it should thicken in seconds.
Toss in peanuts off heat.
p: Kung pao is sweet-sour-numbing in balance: taste the sauce before it hits the wok.

i: 400g flank steak, thin against the grain
Velvet: 1 tsp baking soda + 1 tbsp soy + 1 tbsp cornstarch, 15 min
Sauce: 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sugar, 120ml stock, slurry
m: Sear velveted beef in a ripping-hot pan 1 min; remove.
Fry garlic and ginger; add broccoli and sauce.
Return beef as the sauce thickens to a gloss.
Serve immediately over rice.
p: Baking soda velveting is the takeout secret: 15 minutes turns flank silk-soft.

m: Make a hot-water dough; rest 30 min: it becomes stretchy and forgiving.
Roll thin, brush with oil-flour paste, blanket with scallions and salt.
Roll into a snake, coil into a snail, flatten again. This builds the layers.
Pan-fry in shallow oil, pressing and rotating, until shattering-crisp.
p: Hot water kills gluten's bounce: that's why these roll thin without fighting back.

i: 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sesame oil, white pepper, ginger
1.2L chicken stock + a slice of ginger
m: Beat the filling in one direction until sticky and bouncy.
Dot filling, wet edges, fold triangle, then pinch corners together.
Boil wontons separately until they float + 1 min.
Serve in hot seasoned stock with greens.
p: Boil wontons in water, not the broth; the flour would cloud your clean stock.

i: 200g ground pork fried crisp with 1 tbsp sweet bean or hoisin
Per bowl: 1 tbsp sesame paste or tahini, 1 tbsp chili oil, 2 tsp soy, 1 tsp black vinegar, ½ tsp sugar, ground Sichuan pepper
m: Build the sauce in each serving bowl.
Fry the pork topping until crispy and dark.
Cook noodles; loosen each sauce bowl with 3 tbsp noodle water.
Noodles in, pork on top: everyone mixes their own.
p: The dish is a sauce ratio, not a recipe. Learn it once, riff forever.

i: 2 tbsp soy + 1 tsp sugar + 2 tbsp water, warmed
m: Steam fish over sliced ginger: whole ~10 min, fillets 6–7 min.
Discard steaming liquid; blanket with raw ginger and scallion julienne.
Pour smoking oil over: it should crackle violently.
Drizzle the seasoned soy around, not on, the fish.
p: The hot-oil pour flash-cooks the aromatics. If it doesn't sizzle, the oil wasn't ready.

i: 2L chicken stock or water + bone-in chicken
Toppings: scallion, fried shallots, white pepper, soy, chili crisp, century egg if you're brave
m: Simmer rice, ginger, and chicken gently, lid ajar, 60–90 min, stirring now and then.
Pull chicken when cooked; shred and return.
Cook until the grains burst into silk; thin with stock to taste.
Season lightly; let the toppings do the talking.
p: Freeze the rinsed rice overnight first and it breaks down in half the time.

i: Marinade: juice of 2 limes + 1 orange, 2 tsp each cumin and smoked paprika, oregano, garlic, chipotle in adobo
m: Marinate chicken 30 min to overnight.
Grill or sear hard until charred at the edges; rest, chop.
Toast tortillas on the open flame or dry pan.
Serve street-style: meat, onion, cilantro, lime. Nothing else needed.
p: Double-stack thin tortillas: the inner one catches the juice, the outer stays whole.

m: Mash onion, chili, cilantro, and salt into a rough paste first, a molcajete if you have one.
Fold in avocado, leaving real chunks.
Lime and salt until it tastes bright, then one more pinch of salt.
Serve immediately with the pit in (it doesn't help; it just looks right).
p: Salt suppresses bitterness and makes avocado taste more like itself. Season past timid.

i: 600g chicken breasts or thighs, poached and shredded
Garlic, oregano, splash of poaching broth
m: Caramelize onion; blend tomatoes with chipotles and garlic.
Fry the purée in the onion pan until darkened and thick: this is 'frying the salsa'.
Add chicken and broth; simmer 15 min until juicy, not soupy.
Pile onto tostadas with crema, lettuce, queso.
p: Frying the blended salsa concentrates it: a raw purée tastes like tomato juice, a fried one like Mexico.

i: Tortillas and salsa verde to serve
m: Marinate 30 min: citrus starts 'cooking' the meat beyond that.
Grill over the hottest fire you can make, 3–4 min per side.
Rest 5 min; slice thin against the grain.
Serve as tacos or with beans and grilled onions.
p: Skirt steak has an obvious grain: cut across it and it's butter, with it and it's a chew toy.

m: Boil tomatillos and chilies until olive-drab; blend with aromatics; fry the salsa 10 min.
Flash-fry each tortilla 5 seconds a side to waterproof it.
Dip, fill with chicken, roll seam-down; sauce generously.
Bake 10 min; finish with crema, cheese, raw onion rings.
p: The 5-second fry is non-negotiable: skipped, your enchiladas dissolve into casserole.

i: Garnish bar: cabbage, radish, lime, onion, oregano, tostadas
m: Simmer pork with onion, garlic, bay until tender, ~90 min.
Toast chilies 30 seconds; soak, blend with garlic, strain; fry the purée.
Add chili base and hominy to the pot; simmer 30 min more.
Serve with the garnish bar: the toppings are half the dish.
p: Toast chilies until fragrant, never smoking: burnt chile is bitter forever.

m: Char corn directly over flame or a screaming grill pan, turning, ~8 min.
Paint with the mayo-crema while hot.
Roll in cotija; dust with chile.
Squeeze lime over everything.
p: The mayo is glue and gloss: it's what makes the cheese and chile stick to every kernel.

m: Char poblanos until fully blackened; steam in a bag, peel, slit, seed carefully.
Stuff with cheese; seal with a toothpick; dust with flour.
Whip whites to soft peaks, fold in yolks; coat chilies in this capeado.
Fry in 180°C oil, basting the top, until puffed gold. Serve in warm salsa.
p: The flour dust is primer: egg batter slides straight off a naked chile.

m: Dry-char tomatoes, chilies, garlic, onion on a comal or cast iron until blistered black in spots.
Peel the garlic; grind chilies and garlic with salt first.
Work in tomatoes and onion to a rustic, textured crush.
Finish with cilantro. Never refrigerate what you'll eat today.
p: Char is the seasoning. A pale salsa needs a confession, not more salt.

i: Sponge: 5 eggs, 150g sugar, 120g flour, splash vanilla
250ml cream (in the soak) + more whipped on top
m: Whip eggs and sugar to ribbon stage; fold in flour. Bake 175°C, 25 min.
Cool slightly; stab everywhere with a skewer.
Pour the whisked three milks over slowly, in stages. Chill 4+ hours.
Crown with whipped cream and cinnamon.
p: A fatless sponge is a sponge in the literal sense — butter cakes refuse to drink.

i: 600g chicken thighs, in yogurt + ginger-garlic + chili powder 1h
1 tbsp garam masala, 1 tsp each kasuri methi, sugar
m: Char the marinated chicken hard under a broiler or in a dry pan; set aside.
Simmer tomatoes with aromatics 20 min; blend silky; strain if you're fancy.
Mount with butter and cream; season with garam masala and crushed kasuri methi.
Fold in chicken and its juices; simmer 5 min.
p: Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaf) is the flavor people can't name but always miss.

i: 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp turmeric, chili, 1 tsp amchur or lemon
m: Brown onions properly: 12 patient minutes, deep gold.
Add ginger-garlic, then spices; fry 30 seconds in the fat.
Add tomatoes; cook until the masala pulls away from the pan and the oil rises.
Chickpeas + a cup of water; simmer 15 min, mashing a few. Finish with amchur and cilantro.
p: 'The oil separating' is India's version of deglazing the fond: it's the doneness signal for every masala.

i: Tadka: 3 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 3 garlic cloves sliced, 2 dried chilies, pinch hing, curry leaves if you have them
m: Simmer lentils with turmeric until collapsing; whisk to your preferred texture.
Season with salt; stir in chopped tomato.
Make the tadka: bloom spices in hot ghee until the garlic is bronzed. Seconds matter.
Pour it over the dal at the table. Listen to it.
p: The tadka is added last because fat-bloomed spices lose their perfume in a long simmer.

i: 1 tsp each cumin and garam masala
m: Blend the shocked spinach coarsely: it should stay emerald.
Fry onion, then ginger-garlic-chili, then tomato until the fat rises.
Add spinach; simmer only 5 min to keep the color.
Fold in paneer, cream, methi; done.
p: Blanch-and-shock keeps chlorophyll bright. Long-simmered spinach turns army green.

i: 600g chicken thighs in yogurt + biryani masala + ginger-garlic
Whole spices: bay, cardamom, cinnamon, clove
m: Parboil rice with whole spices to 70%; a grain should snap, not squash.
Layer: marinated chicken on the bottom, rice, birista, herbs, saffron milk, ghee.
Seal the lid (foil or dough); 10 min medium, then 25 min lowest heat (dum).
Rest 10 min. Dig from the bottom up.
p: 70% rice is the whole exam: it finishes in the steam. Fully cooked rice becomes porridge upstairs.

i: 1 tsp cumin seeds, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander, garam masala
m: Sear cauliflower and potato in oil until spotted brown; remove.
Bloom cumin; fry onion, ginger, chili; add ground spices and tomato.
Return vegetables; splash of water, lid on, 12 min.
Uncover, dry it out, finish with garam masala and cilantro.
p: This is a dry curry: steam to cook, then evaporate. A wet aloo gobi is a stew that lost its way.

m: Whisk yogurt smooth with a splash of water.
Squeeze the cucumber like you mean it.
Fold everything together; dust with cumin and chili.
p: Roast whole cumin in a dry pan, then grind: pre-ground is a photocopy of the smell.

i: 1 tsp each sugar, salt; ½ tsp baking soda + 1 tsp baking powder (or 4g yeast)
m: Knead a soft, slightly tacky dough; rest 1 hour covered.
Roll teardrops; wet one side with water.
Slap wet-side down onto a ripping-hot dry cast iron; when bubbled, flip the pan over the open flame to char the top.
Brush with garlic butter immediately.
p: The water-slap makes the naan stick like a tandoor wall: that's how you get flame-kissed bubbles at home.

i: 8 chicken drumsticks/thighs, slashed to the bone
Marinade 2: thick yogurt, ginger-garlic, garam masala, cumin, turmeric, kashmiri chili, mustard oil
Butter for basting, onion + lime to serve
m: Two-stage marinade: acid first, then yogurt mix 4–24 h.
Roast at 240°C on a rack ~25 min, or grill.
Baste with butter; finish under the broiler until charred at the ridges.
Rest; serve with lime, raw onion, mint chutney.
p: Slashes let marinade and heat reach the bone: unslashed tandoori is just baked chicken in costume.

m: Simmer rice in milk, stirring often, scraping the sides in, 40 min.
It's ready when a spoon leaves a trail.
Sweeten at the end; add cardamom and saffron.
Chill or serve warm, heavy with nuts.
p: The browned milk solids on the pot wall are flavor: scrape them back in, don't fight them.

i: 200g dried rice noodles, soaked in warm water 30 min
Sauce: 3 tbsp tamarind paste, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp palm sugar
Firm tofu, dried shrimp, garlic chives, bean sprouts
m: Cook the sauce until it tastes equally sweet, sour, salty.
Wok in two batches: sear protein and tofu, push aside, scramble egg.
Add noodles and sauce; toss until noodles absorb it and turn supple.
Sprouts and chives at the last second; peanuts and lime at the table.
p: Soak, don't boil, the noodles: they finish cooking in the sauce and stay chewy, not mushy.

i: 4 tbsp green curry paste (jarred is fine, doctor with fresh chili and lime leaf)
m: Fry the paste in the thick coconut cream from the can's top until the oil splits out, 5 min.
Add chicken; coat in the paste.
Add remaining coconut milk, eggplant, torn lime leaves; simmer 12 min.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar; rain in basil off heat.
p: 'Cracking' the coconut cream, frying until oil separates, is the step that separates Thai kitchens from timid ones.

i: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp lime juice
Thai chilies, cilantro, chili paste (nam prik pao) optional
m: Simmer the aromatics in stock 10 min: they flavor, you don't eat them.
Add mushrooms, then shrimp for the last 2 min.
Kill the heat, THEN add lime juice and fish sauce.
Adjust to hot-sour-salty balance; cilantro to finish.
p: Lime juice boiled turns bitter and flat. Off-heat acid is the rule for the whole cuisine.

i: 2 tbsp uncooked sticky rice, toasted and ground (khao khua)
3 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp fish sauce
m: Toast rice in a dry pan to deep gold; grind coarse.
Cook chicken with a splash of water, breaking fine.
Dress warm with lime, fish sauce, chili.
Fold in herbs and rice powder just before serving.
p: Khao khua is nutty perfume plus grip: it's why larb clings to lettuce instead of raining out.

i: 1 tbsp each oyster sauce, fish sauce; 1 tsp dark soy, 1 tsp sugar
Big bunch holy basil (Thai basil works)
Fried egg per person, jasmine rice
m: Scream-hot wok: fry the garlic-chili paste 15 seconds.
Add pork, pressing into the wok to sear, not stew.
Sauces in; toss 1 min.
Off heat, wilt in the basil. Crown rice with it and a crispy-edged fried egg.
p: This is Thailand's 10-minute answer to a bad day. The egg's crispy lace edge is mandatory.

m: Crack the coconut cream; fry the paste and whole spices until fragrant.
Add beef, remaining coconut milk, water to cover; simmer 90 min.
Add potatoes and onion, 25 min more.
Balance: tamarind sour, palm sugar sweet, fish sauce salt. Peanuts in at the end.
p: Massaman is Thai-Persian fusion 300 years old: the warm spices aren't a mistake, they're the history.

i: 2 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp lime, 1 tbsp palm sugar
m: Pound garlic and chilies in a mortar.
Add beans and tomatoes; bruise, don't purée.
Add papaya; pound-and-scoop with a spoon in the other hand to mix.
Dress and taste; it should slap: hot, sour, funky, a little sweet.
p: Pound to bruise. Bruised cells drink dressing; chopped ones just wear it.

i: 1½ tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp soy, pinch sugar
Cucumber, lime, prik nam pla (fish sauce + chilies)
m: Sear protein; scramble eggs in the same wok.
Rice in; press, flip, press over max heat.
Season with fish sauce and soy around the rim.
Serve with cucumber slices, lime, and prik nam pla on the side.
p: Jasmine + fish sauce is what makes it Thai, not Chinese — that and the lime you squeeze at the end.

i: 600g chicken thigh, strips, on soaked skewers
Marinade: coconut milk, turmeric, coriander, cumin, lemongrass, sugar
Sauce: 4 tbsp peanut butter, 200ml coconut milk, 1 tbsp red curry paste, tamarind, palm sugar, fish sauce
m: Marinate 2–24 h.
Simmer sauce ingredients 10 min until it thickens; loosen with water.
Grill skewers hot and fast, brushing with coconut milk.
Serve with sauce and quick-pickled cucumber.
p: Fry the curry paste into the coconut milk first: the sauce goes from peanut butter dip to satay sauce.

m: Steam soaked rice over cloth 25 min: steam, never boil.
Dissolve sugar and salt into warm coconut milk; pour ⅔ over the hot rice; rest 20 min covered.
Salt the remaining coconut milk lightly for the sauce.
Serve warm rice, cold mango, sauce over everything.
p: The salt isn't optional: Thai desserts run on the sweet-salty axis.

i: 2 cans chickpeas (or 250g dried, cooked soft with ½ tsp baking soda)
m: Simmer canned chickpeas 15 min with a pinch of baking soda until squashable; a few skins will float off.
Blend hot chickpeas with garlic and lemon first.
Add tahini; stream in ice water until pale, whipped, and pourable.
Plate in swooshes; flood with olive oil.
p: Hot chickpeas + ice water is the fluffiness hack: the temperature shock whips the tahini.

i: 1 tsp baking powder, 2 tbsp flour if needed
Oil for deep frying; tahini sauce, pita, pickles
m: Grind soaked (uncooked!) chickpeas with everything to coarse couscous texture.
Rest 30 min; stir in baking powder.
Form balls; fry at 175°C until deep brown, ~4 min.
Stuff into pita with salad, pickles, tahini.
p: Canned chickpeas make falafel that explodes into the oil. Dried-and-soaked is a law, not a preference.

i: 1 tsp each cumin and paprika, pinch cayenne
m: Soften onion and pepper 10 min; add garlic and spices.
Add tomatoes; simmer 10 min until thick enough to hold a spoon-well.
Crack eggs into wells; cover and cook 6–8 min to runny yolks.
Feta, herbs, bread. Serve in the pan.
p: Thicken the sauce before the eggs go in: eggs poached in watery sauce turn the whole pan to soup.

i: Marinade: 4 tbsp olive oil, lemon, 6 garlic cloves, 2 tsp each cumin and paprika, 1 tsp turmeric, ½ tsp cinnamon, pinch allspice
Pita, tahini or garlic sauce (toum), pickles
m: Marinate 1–24 h.
Roast at 220°C with the onions, 30–35 min, until charred at the edges.
Rest, slice thin, then crisp the slices in the pan juices under the broiler 3 min.
Pile into pita with sauce and pickles.
p: The slice-then-broil step fakes the rotating spit: maximum crispy edges per bite.

i: 3 big bunches flat parsley, chopped fine and dry
3 tbsp fine bulgur, soaked in the tomato juices
Lemon juice, olive oil, salt, pinch allspice
m: Wash and DRY the parsley completely before chopping.
Dice tomatoes; let bulgur soak in their juice 15 min, no cooking.
Chop parsley with a sharp knife; bruised parsley turns to lawn clippings.
Combine; dress sharply with lemon.
p: Real tabbouleh is a parsley salad with bulgur in it, not the other way around.

i: 2 pitas, torn and fried or toasted crisp
Dressing: lemon, olive oil, garlic, 2 tsp sumac
m: Crisp the pita in olive oil; salt it like chips.
Chop vegetables chunky; herbs whole-leaf.
Whisk dressing heavy on sumac and lemon.
Toss with pita at the last moment.
p: Sumac is the identity of this salad: lemony, winey, brick-red. Don't sub it out.

i: 1 tsp each cumin, coriander, allspice; ½ tsp cinnamon
m: Knead meat, onion, herbs, spices until tacky: the protein binds itself.
Chill 30 min; form onto skewers, pressing finger-dents.
Grill or broil hot, 3–4 min per side.
Serve on flatbread with yogurt and sumac onions.
p: Grate-and-squeeze the onion: flavor without the water that makes kofta fall off the skewer.

m: Burn the eggplants (whole, directly on flame or under broiler) until collapsed and blackened all over, ~20 min.
Drain the flesh in a colander 15 min; discard the bitter liquid.
Chop-and-stir with tahini, lemon, garlic. Fork, not blender.
Pool olive oil on top; jewel with pomegranate.
p: The smoke IS the recipe. Un-charred eggplant makes tahini-flavored baby food.

m: Fry onions low and slow in generous oil until deep mahogany and half-crisp, 25 min. Reserve half.
Simmer lentils 12 min; add rice, cumin, water to cover by 2cm.
Fold in half the onions; cook covered 15 min, rest 10.
Crown with the crispy onions and cold yogurt.
p: This peasant dish lives or dies on onion patience. Mahogany, not blond.

i: 250g walnuts or pistachios, ground with cinnamon
Syrup: 200g sugar, 150ml water, honey, lemon, made FIRST and cooled
m: Butter 2 sheets, scatter nuts, roll around a dowel or loosely by hand; scrunch into the pan.
Repeat until the pan is full; butter the tops; slice now, not later.
Bake 170°C, 40 min, to deep gold.
Pour COLD syrup over HOT pastry: listen to it crackle.
p: Cold syrup + hot pastry = crisp. Hot syrup + hot pastry = soggy. It's physics, not opinion.

m: Poach, not fry, potatoes and onion in the oil over medium-low until tender, 20 min.
Drain well; fold into beaten, well-salted eggs; rest 10 min.
Cook in a nonstick pan over medium 4 min; plate-flip; 3 min more.
Serve jiggly in the center, at room temperature, with pride.
p: The plate-flip is a rite of passage. Commit fully: hesitation is how tortillas hit the floor.

i: 320g bomba or calasparra rice (arborio in a pinch)
Chicken thighs, chorizo optional (heresy but delicious), shrimp
Sofrito: onion, garlic, grated tomato, 1 tsp pimentón
m: Brown chicken; make the sofrito in the same pan until jammy.
Add rice; toast 1 min. Add all the hot saffron stock. NOW STOP STIRRING.
Simmer 18 min, rotating the pan; add shrimp for the last 5.
Crank the heat 90 seconds for socarrat, the crackling bottom crust. Rest 5 min under a towel.
p: Stirring makes risotto. Not stirring makes paella. The socarrat is the reward for restraint.

i: 1 dried guindilla or chile de árbol
m: Warm oil, garlic, and chili from cold: the garlic should toast slowly to pale gold.
Raise the heat; shrimp in a single layer, 45 seconds a side.
Splash of sherry; parsley.
Serve bubbling with bread for the oil, which is the actual point.
p: Starting garlic in cold oil is how you get 8 cloves of flavor with zero bitterness.

i: Brava sauce: olive oil, 2 tsp pimentón (mix sweet+hot), 1 tbsp flour, 250ml stock, splash vinegar
Optional allioli: garlic + oil emulsion or garlicky mayo
m: Simmer potatoes 8 min; dry completely; chill if you have time.
Fry twice: 150°C until tender, then 190°C until shattering.
Brava: bloom pimentón in oil, stir in flour, whisk in stock until it coats a spoon; vinegar to finish.
Sauce over, never under: the crunch must survive.
p: Double-frying is the same physics as great French fries: cook first, crust second.

i: 100ml good olive oil, 2 tbsp sherry vinegar
m: Blend vegetables, bread, vinegar until totally smooth, minutes, not seconds.
With the motor running, stream in the oil; watch it turn pale coral and creamy.
Chill 2 hours; adjust salt and vinegar cold (cold mutes both).
Serve in a glass. It's a drink that ate a salad.
p: The oil emulsion is what separates gazpacho from cold salsa: don't skip the slow stream.

m: Grill or toast the bread hard.
Ghost the garlic clove across the hot surface once or twice.
Grate the tomato halves on a box grater; discard skins. Spoon over.
Oil generously; salt; eat immediately.
p: Four ingredients means zero hiding places. This dish is a quality test for all of them.

i: Bread soaked in milk, 1 egg, garlic, parsley
Sauce: onion, carrot, garlic, 150ml white wine, 400ml stock, saffron or pimentón
Almond picada (optional): ground almonds + fried bread + garlic
m: Mix meatballs gently; roll in flour; brown, don't cook through.
Build the sauce in the same pan; blend it smooth if you like.
Simmer meatballs in the sauce 20 min.
Thicken with the picada, Spain's ancient answer to cornstarch.
p: The flour coating browns into the fond that becomes your sauce. Nothing is wasted.

i: 1 chicken, cut in small pieces (or 8 thighs)
m: Brown chicken hard in olive oil with the garlic cloves loitering around it.
When garlic is bronzed and chicken golden, add sherry and herbs.
Simmer uncovered 20 min, turning, until the sauce is a garlicky glaze.
Serve with bread and the confit garlic to squeeze out.
p: Skin-on smashed garlic perfumes without burning; naked minced garlic would be charcoal by minute five.

m: Make a blond roux; whisk in milk gradually into a THICK béchamel, 15 min of stirring.
Fold in ham; spread in a tray, press film onto the surface; chill 4h+.
Shape logs; bread twice (egg, panko, egg, panko).
Fry at 185°C in small batches until deep gold, ~2 min.
p: The béchamel should be almost too thick to stir: it loosens into molten cream inside the crust.

i: Lemon peel, orange peel, cinnamon stick
m: Infuse milk with citrus peel and cinnamon 15 min; strain.
Whisk yolks, sugar, cornstarch; temper in milk; return to the stove.
Stir until it thickens to loose pudding: first bubble, then off.
Chill in shallow dishes; burn a sugar crust with a torch or screaming-hot spoon.
p: Crème brûlée's older cousin: stovetop, citrus-and-cinnamon, and done in half the time, no oven, no water bath.

i: 1 green pepper, rings; ½ red onion
Oregano, red wine vinegar, lots of olive oil
m: Chunk everything rustic; no lettuce, ever.
Salt the tomatoes first and let them weep a little.
Dress with vinegar and a fearless pour of oil.
Lay the feta slab on top whole; dust with oregano.
p: The tomato juice + oil + vinegar pooling at the bottom is the sauce. Bread goes in it. That's the meal.

i: 1 cucumber, grated, salted, and strangled dry
2 tbsp olive oil, splash red wine vinegar
m: Salt the grated cucumber 10 min, then squeeze in a towel until it gives up.
Fold everything into the yogurt.
Rest 30 min: the garlic needs time to bloom.
Trench of olive oil on top to serve.
p: Watery tzatziki is a squeezing failure, never a recipe failure.

i: Marinade: olive oil, lemon, garlic, 2 tsp oregano, 1 tsp honey
m: Marinate 30 min–8 h.
Thread snugly; grill or broil hot, turning, ~12 min, until charred at the corners.
Warm pitas over the same flame.
Build: pita, tzatziki, meat, tomato, onion, more oregano.
p: Oregano + lemon + char is the entire flavor thesis of the Greek grill. Honey helps the char along.

i: Ragù: 600g lamb or beef, onion, garlic, tomato, red wine, cinnamon stick, allspice
Béchamel: 80g butter, 80g flour, 800ml milk, nutmeg, 2 yolks, grated cheese
m: Roast the sliced vegetables until golden instead of frying: lighter, faster.
Cook the ragù until thick and jammy; cinnamon is the signature, don't fear it.
Make a thick béchamel; enrich with yolks and cheese off heat.
Layer potato, eggplant, ragù, béchamel deep on top. Bake 180°C, 45 min. REST 30 MIN.
p: Moussaka cut hot is soup. The 30-minute rest is written in stone on an island somewhere.

i: 1 pack phyllo, 150g melted butter or olive oil
m: Mix filling; it should be dry enough to mound.
Layer half the phyllo sheets in a buttered pan, brushing each.
Filling in; layer remaining sheets, brushing each. Score the top now.
Bake 180°C, 45 min, to deep gold. Cool 15 min.
p: Wet spinach is the enemy of crisp phyllo. Squeeze, then squeeze again, then once more.

m: Cook orzo in the stock; add chicken.
Whisk eggs and lemon until frothy.
Temper: whisk hot broth into the eggs one ladle at a time, then pour back off the heat.
Warm gently, never boil again, until it turns velvet.
p: Tempering is the technique; the reward is a soup thickened by nothing but egg, lemon, and nerve.

m: Toss everything with the grated tomato, oil, and seasoning.
Layer or jumble into a baking dish; sliced tomato on top.
Bake 190°C for 60–75 min, until collapsed, blistered, and syrupy at the edges.
Room temperature with feta and bread.
p: Greek vegetable dishes use oil as an ingredient, not a coating. Lathera means 'the oily ones'; lean in.

m: Whisk the liquid, oil, lemon, mustard; toss with potatoes in a roasting pan.
Roast 200°C for 40 min in the braise.
Liquid gone? Now they fry in the leftover oil: 20 more minutes, turning once.
They should be creamy inside, bronzed and lemon-lacquered outside.
p: Braise-then-roast is the trick: the potatoes drink the lemon first, then crisp in what remains.

i: Stale bread soaked in milk (or 3 tbsp breadcrumbs)
m: Knead everything; rest the mix 30 min in the fridge.
Roll walnut-size; dust in flour.
Shallow-fry in olive oil until crusty and deep brown.
Lemon over the top. Serve with tzatziki.
p: Mint is what makes them Greek. Skip it and you've made good meatballs from nowhere in particular.

i: ½ green chili or pinch chili flakes
Foil or a small clay dish; bread
m: Layer tomato, feta, chili in a small dish; oil and oregano over.
Bake 200°C for 12–15 min until slumped and bubbling at the edges.
Optional 1-min broil for color.
Attack with bread while molten.
p: Feta doesn't melt like mozzarella: it softens to a spreadable cloud. That's the texture you want.

i: The trinity: 2 onions, 2 celery ribs, 1 green pepper, diced
m: Make a dark roux: whisk oil and flour over medium 30–45 min to milk-chocolate brown. Do not walk away.
Trinity into the hot roux — it will roar and stop the cooking.
Whisk in stock gradually; add browned sausage and chicken; simmer 1 hour.
Skim, season, scallions. Serve over rice.
p: The roux is a color, not a time. Chocolate roux = deep gumbo. Blond roux = étouffée. Burnt roux = start over, no appeals.

i: 1 smoked ham hock or 300g pickled pork/smoked sausage
Bay, thyme, cayenne, black + white pepper
m: Sweat the trinity; add garlic, seasoning, beans, hock, water to cover well.
Simmer 2–3 hours until beans surrender.
Mash a cupful against the pot wall to cream the gravy.
Serve over rice with sliced sausage seared crisp and hot sauce on the table.
p: Monday food: it simmers while you live your life. Creaminess comes from the mash, not from cream.

m: Brown sausage, then chicken, hard: the crust on the pot bottom is the flavor bank.
Trinity in; scrape up every brown bit.
Rice, stock, seasoning; boil, then lid on, lowest heat, 25 min. NO PEEKING.
Rest 10, fold from the bottom, scallions over.
p: Brown = Cajun, red = Creole; both are correct and both camps will tell you the other is wrong.

i: 600g shrimp (make quick stock from the shells)
m: Simmer shells in water 15 min; strain. Free flavor.
Butter roux to peanut-butter color; trinity in.
Whisk in stock to a gravy; season; simmer 15 min.
Shrimp in for the final 3 minutes only. Over rice.
p: Étouffée means 'smothered': the shrimp poach in the gravy, so they go in last or they go in vain.

i: 250g chicken livers + 250g ground pork (or all pork)
m: Sear the pork; add finely chopped livers and cook until deeply browned.
Trinity in the same fat; scrape the fond.
Fold in the rice with splashes of stock so it stains 'dirty'.
Scallions and parsley heavy at the end.
p: The livers are the 'dirt': mineral depth people love until you tell them what it is. Tell them after.

m: Sweat the trinity in butter; garlic and seasonings after.
Tomatoes in; simmer 20 min to a bright, loose sauce.
Balance: hot sauce, Worcestershire, pinch of sugar if the tomatoes bite.
Shrimp for 4 minutes at the end; over rice.
p: No roux here: Creole cooking shows its French-Spanish-African braid with tomato instead.

i: Blackening mix: 1 tbsp paprika, 2 tsp cayenne, thyme, oregano, garlic + onion powder, black + white pepper, salt
Cast iron, outdoors or with the windows open
m: Heat dry cast iron until it's genuinely frightening, 10 minutes.
Dip fillets in butter; pack the spice on both sides.
Lay in the pan: 2–3 min per side. It will smoke like a rite.
More butter and lemon over the crust to serve.
p: Paul Prudhomme's dish nearly wiped out the redfish it made famous. The 'blackening' is butter and spice charring, not fish burning.

i: 1 round seeded muffuletta loaf or sturdy Italian bread
Olive salad: green olives, giardiniera, celery, capers, garlic, oregano, olive oil — chopped, ideally rested overnight
m: Chop the olive salad fine; let it marinate as long as you can stand.
Split the loaf; spoon oil and salad onto BOTH cut faces.
Layer meats and cheeses generously.
Press under a weight 30 min; cut in quarters. Room temperature is correct.
p: The pressing lets the olive oil soak the crumb: a fresh muffuletta is good; a pressed one is legendary.

i: Oil for frying; an avalanche of powdered sugar
m: Make a soft, slightly sticky dough; rise 1–2 h (or overnight cold, better).
Roll 1cm thick; cut rectangles; no second proof needed.
Fry at 180°C, flipping, until puffed and gold, ~2 min per side.
Bury in powdered sugar while hot. No restraint permitted.
p: They puff into pillows because of the rolled dough's trapped layers of gas. Fry immediately after cutting.

m: Melt butter and sugar into a bubbling caramel; add cinnamon.
Bananas in, 1 min per side, basting.
Off heat, add rum; return to flame and tilt to ignite (or just simmer 1 min, still delicious).
Over cold ice cream immediately.
p: Born at Brennan's in 1951. If you flambé: long lighter, pan off the burner, and nothing above the pan you love.

i: 1.5 cups sour, well-fermented kimchi, chopped + 3 tbsp of its juice
1 tbsp gochujang, 1 tsp soy, sesame oil
Fried egg per person, scallions, sesame, nori
m: Render the pork; fry kimchi in the fat 3 min until its edges catch.
Rice in; press and toss with gochujang and kimchi juice.
Sesame oil off heat.
Fried egg on top, yolk runny; scissors on the nori.
p: Old, sour kimchi is the good stuff for frying — fresh kimchi is for eating cold.

i: 600g ribeye or sirloin, shaved thin (freeze 1h to slice)
Marinade: 4 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, ½ grated Asian pear or apple, garlic, ginger
m: Marinate the shaved beef 30 min–4 h; the pear tenderizes.
Sear in a blazing pan in thin batches so it caramelizes instead of boils.
Sear the onions and mushrooms in the drippings.
Serve as ssam: lettuce, rice, meat, dab of ssamjang, one perfect bite.
p: Grated pear is Korea's ancient meat tenderizer, enzymes plus sweetness in one ingredient.

i: Namul: spinach, bean sprouts, carrots, mushrooms, zucchini; each seasoned separately with sesame oil, garlic, salt
Sauce: 3 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp each sesame oil, sugar, water, vinegar
m: Blanch or sauté each vegetable alone; season each alone. This is the discipline of the dish.
Arrange spokes of color over the rice.
Egg in the center; sauce on the side.
Destroy the arrangement completely before eating: mixing IS the dish (bibim = mix).
p: For dolsot-style: rub a hot stone or cast-iron bowl with sesame oil and let the rice crackle into a crust first.

i: Spinach, carrots, onion, mushrooms, each cooked separately
Sauce: 4 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp sesame oil
m: Boil noodles 6 min; rinse, snip a few times with scissors, toss with a little sauce.
Cook each vegetable and the beef separately, seasoning as you go.
Combine everything with the remaining sauce: hands in gloves work best.
Serve warm or room temp, glistening.
p: Separate sautéing keeps each color and texture distinct: japchae made in one pan tastes beige.

i: Scallions, onion, 500ml water or anchovy stock
m: Fry pork belly until its fat runs; add kimchi and fry 5 min more.
Add pastes, water, onion; boil hard 15 min — jjigae likes violence.
Tofu slabs in gently for the last 5.
Scallions; serve volcanic with rice.
p: The frying step turns sour kimchi's sharpness into depth. Boiled-only jjigae tastes thin.

i: 1kg chicken wings or boneless thigh chunks
Batter: ½ cup potato starch + ¼ cup flour + ½ tsp baking powder + cold water
Sauce: 3 tbsp gochujang, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp each soy, rice vinegar; garlic, butter knob
m: Toss chicken in a thin, drippy batter.
Fry once at 165°C, 8 min; rest 5.
Fry again at 190°C until shattering, 4 min.
Toss in the warmed sauce or serve it alongside to preserve maximum crunch.
p: Potato starch + double fry is why KFC (the Korean one) stays crisp under sauce for an hour.

i: 1 cup flour + ¼ cup potato starch
Whole bunch of scallions, split lengthwise
m: Whisk a thin batter: lumps are fine, cold is critical.
Lay scallions in a hot oiled pan like lumber; pour batter over and around.
Press seafood in; drizzle beaten egg at the edges.
Flip when deeply crisp; crisp side two. Cut with scissors.
p: Ice water and minimal mixing = crisp. Warm water and enthusiasm = pancake sadness.

i: 500g cylindrical rice cakes (soaked 20 min if refrigerated)
2 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp gochugaru, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp soy
m: Dissolve the pastes into the stock; bring to a boil.
Rice cakes and fish cakes in; simmer 10–12 min, stirring so nothing welds to the pot.
The sauce should reduce to a glossy, spicy lava that coats.
Eggs and scallions in the final minutes.
p: The dish is done when the sauce clings: watery tteokbokki just means three more minutes of patience.

i: 1kg flanken-cut beef short ribs (across the bone, thin)
Marinade: 6 tbsp soy, 3 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp mirin, ½ pear grated, garlic, ginger, sesame oil
m: Rinse ribs briefly to shed bone dust; pat dry.
Marinate 4–24 hours.
Grill over high flame 3–4 min per side until lacquered and charred at the edges.
Scissors into segments; wrap in lettuce or attack directly.
p: Flanken cut means each slice owns three little bone medallions: the meat nearest them is the prize.

m: Dissolve doenjang into the stock; add potato first, 5 min.
Everything else except tofu; simmer 10 min.
Tofu and chili last 3 min.
Serve bubbling with rice; this is Korea's daily default dinner.
p: Doenjang is Korea's miso but louder: funkier, chunkier, and it can take a real boil, unlike miso.

i: 1.5L good chicken stock + 2 chicken breasts poached in it
1 onion + big knob ginger, charred over flame
Spices, toasted: 2 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 cloves, 1 tsp coriander seed
Fish sauce, rock sugar or pinch sugar
Herb plate: Thai basil, cilantro, lime, sprouts, chilies, hoisin, sriracha
m: Char onion and ginger until blackened; toast spices; add both to stock.
Simmer 30 min; strain; season with fish sauce and sugar until it tastes complete alone.
Cook noodles separately; slice the poached chicken.
Bowl: noodles, chicken, boiling broth over. Herbs at the table, each to their own.
p: Charring the aromatics is pho's signature: sweet smoke in the broth that no shortcut replaces.

i: Grilled lemongrass pork or chicken (marinade: lemongrass, fish sauce, sugar, garlic, shallot)
Do chua: carrot + daikon, quick-pickled in vinegar-sugar-salt 30 min
Cucumber spears, cilantro sprigs, sliced chili, Maggi or soy
m: Pickle the vegetables first: they need 30 minutes minimum.
Grill the marinated meat until caramelized at the edges.
Toast the roll hollow-hot; paint with mayo (and pâté).
Layer meat, pickles, cucumber, whole cilantro sprigs, chilies, a shake of Maggi.
p: The architecture is contrast: warm/cool, rich/pickled, crisp/soft. Missing pickles collapses the whole thesis.

i: 500g pork shoulder, thin slices, marinated: lemongrass, fish sauce, sugar, garlic, shallot, sesame oil
Lettuce, cucumber, herbs (mint, perilla, cilantro), pickled carrot-daikon
m: Grill or sear the pork hard until the sugar chars, in batches.
Build bowls: lettuce and herbs at the bottom, noodles, pork on top.
Peanuts and fried shallots over.
Nuoc cham poured over everything at the table; toss like a salad.
p: It's a noodle salad, not a noodle soup: cold noodles, hot meat, cool herbs, and the sauce ties the room together.

i: Cooked shrimp, halved lengthwise (and/or pork belly slices)
Peanut dip: hoisin + peanut butter + a little water, chili, crushed peanuts
m: Dip rice paper in warm water 2 seconds; it keeps softening after, so undershoot.
Lay shrimp pink-side-down first, then herbs, lettuce, noodles.
Fold sides, then roll tight like a burrito.
Serve seam-down with the peanut sauce.
p: Two-second dip. The paper should still feel slightly stiff when you start rolling.

i: 3 tbsp sugar (for the caramel, nuoc mau)
Black pepper, chilies, scallion; clay pot ideal
m: Melt sugar dry to a dark amber caramel, darker than feels safe.
Add fish sauce (stand back), aromatics, and a splash of coconut water.
Nestle in the fish; simmer uncovered 20–25 min, spooning the sauce over.
Finish aggressive with black pepper. Rice is not optional.
p: Bitter-edge caramel + fish sauce is the backbone of Vietnamese kho: sweet, salty, smoky, profound.

i: 3 stalks lemongrass, tender parts minced fine
Turmeric ½ tsp (optional, for the golden version)
m: Marinate chicken 15 min in everything.
Sear in a hot pan without crowding until the edges caramelize.
Add a splash of water to glaze; reduce until sticky.
Over rice with cucumber and extra chili.
p: Mince lemongrass like you're angry at it: big pieces are woody splinters, fine mince is pure perfume.

i: Garlic, minced; bird's eye chili; shreds of carrot
m: Dissolve sugar in warm water.
Add fish sauce and lime; adjust until no single note dominates.
Garlic and chili float on top when it's mixed right.
Keeps a week; you'll use it on everything.
p: This is the master sauce of the cuisine: learn the ratio (1:1:⅔:2) and you can dress a nation of dishes.

i: 3 tbsp dark roast coffee, coarse (robusta traditional)
Phin filter (or moka pot / strong French press)
m: Condensed milk in the glass first.
Brew the coffee slowly through the phin directly on top: 4–5 minutes of drips.
Stir hard to marry them.
Pour over ice. Sit with it.
p: Robusta's brutal strength is the point — condensed milk was built to argue with it.

i: 1 big bunch morning glory (water spinach) — or substitute spinach/broccolini
1 tbsp fish sauce (or soy for veg)
m: Split thick stems; keep leaves whole.
Blast garlic in hot oil 10 seconds.
Greens in, tossing violently; fish sauce and sugar around the rim.
90 seconds total. Out before it weeps.
p: The wok should be hot enough that the greens hiss like rain on pavement. Anything gentler stews them.

i: Huge knob ginger, half julienned, half smashed
m: Make the dark caramel; add fish sauce and shallots.
Chicken and smashed ginger in; coat, splash of water.
Simmer uncovered 25 min, turning, until the sauce is a dark glaze.
Julienned ginger and pepper in the last 5 minutes so it stays fiery.
p: Two ginger additions, two jobs: early ginger mellows into the sauce; late ginger keeps its bite.

i: 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp each ginger and turmeric, pinch saffron
m: Coat chicken in the spices and grated onion; rest 30 min.
Brown gently; add water halfway up; simmer covered 45 min.
Uncover, reduce; add olives and preserved lemon for the last 10.
The sauce should be thick, yellow, and glossy with onion.
p: Grated onion melts into the sauce entirely; that body is the tagine's signature, no flour needed.

i: 2 onions, 1 tsp each ginger, cinnamon; ½ tsp turmeric; saffron
m: Brown lamb; soften onions with the spices.
Water to nearly cover; simmer very low 2 hours until spoon-tender.
Apricots and honey in for the last 20 min.
Scatter almonds and sesame; serve from the pot.
p: Sweet-savory is Morocco's home key: the apricots should read as depth, not dessert. Balance with salt.

i: Vegetables: carrot, turnip, zucchini, pumpkin, cabbage, tomato, onion
Broth: ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, saffron, olive oil
Raisins, smen or butter, harissa on the side
m: Simmer the sturdier vegetables in the spiced broth 20 min; softer ones in the final 10.
Steam or hydrate the couscous; fluff with butter, grain by grain.
Mound couscous, crater the top, vegetables in and around.
Broth over; harissa thinned with broth for those who dare.
p: Friday couscous is a ritual across the Maghreb: the broth-soaked mound matters more than any single vegetable.

i: 1 tsp each ginger, turmeric, cinnamon; pepper
Tedouira: 2 tbsp flour whisked in water; lemon, dates on the side
m: Brown lamb with onion, celery, spices.
Tomatoes, lentils, water; simmer 40 min; chickpeas in.
Stream in the flour slurry, stirring, to a silky, faintly thick body.
Herb avalanche at the end; serve with lemon and dates, Ramadan-style.
p: The tedouira slurry gives harira its signature velvet: thin soup is missing the step, not the point.

i: 4 white fish fillets or 1 whole fish
Chermoula: big bunch cilantro + parsley, 4 garlic cloves, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika, pinch cayenne, lemon juice, olive oil, blended
m: Blend the chermoula; use a third to marinate the fish 20 min.
Layer sliced vegetables in a dish; toss with another third; roast 20 min at 210°C.
Fish on top, remaining chermoula over; back in for 12–15 min.
Serve from the dish with bread.
p: Chermoula is Morocco's pesto: marinade, sauce, and dressing in one. Make double, always.

i: 2 eggplants, charred whole or cubed and steamed
m: Cook garlic in olive oil; add tomatoes and spices; reduce to a jam.
Mash in the eggplant flesh; keep cooking until thick enough to stand a spoon.
Finish with lemon and cilantro.
Warm or room temp, with bread, as part of a salad spread.
p: Moroccan 'salads' are mostly cooked and served in a mosaic of small plates: zaalouk anchors the table.

i: 500g ground beef or lamb, kneaded with grated onion, cumin, paprika, parsley, cilantro
Sauce: 800g tomatoes, garlic, 1 tsp paprika, ½ tsp cumin, pinch cayenne
m: Roll small marble-size kefta.
Simmer the tomato sauce 15 min until thick; drop kefta straight in raw; 15 min more.
Crack eggs into the bubbling sauce; cover 5 min to just-set.
Serve in the tagine or pan; eat with bread only, no cutlery.
p: Poaching the raw meatballs in the sauce trades a browning step for tenderness, and one less pan.

i: 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp paprika, pinch cayenne
m: Boil carrots 6–8 min; drain hot.
Toss immediately with garlic, spices, lemon, oil.
Rest 30 min minimum; better after a night.
Shower with herbs to serve, room temperature.
p: Warm vegetables drink dressing: the same trick as the Niçoise potatoes, wearing a djellaba.

i: Sugar to a level that would alarm your dentist (adjust)
Boiling water; a pot with a long spout
m: Rinse the tea leaves with a splash of boiling water; discard the rinse (it removes bitterness).
Add mint and sugar; fill with boiling water; steep 3–4 min.
Pour a glass and return it to the pot, twice, to mix.
Pour from a height for the crown of foam. That foam is the honor of the house.
p: The high pour aerates and cools, and hospitality is measured in the foam it leaves.

i: Mint, chopped dates or almonds optional
m: Peel oranges to the flesh; slice into wheels, catching juice.
Arrange; sprinkle with orange-blossom water and sugar.
Dust cinnamon in stripes.
Chill 20 min; mint on top.
p: Five minutes, four ingredients, and it ends a heavy tagine like a window opening.

i: Brine: 500ml buttermilk, 2 tbsp salt, hot sauce, 4–24 h
Dredge: 300g flour + 50g cornstarch, paprika, garlic powder, cayenne, black pepper, salt
Oil for frying (cast iron, 2cm deep, or a pot)
m: Pull chicken from buttermilk; dredge hard, pressing craggy bits on. Rest 15 min so the crust hydrates.
Fry at 160–165°C, turning, 14–18 min to 74°C internal at the bone.
Rest on a rack, never paper towels.
Salt the second it leaves the oil.
p: The 15-minute post-dredge rest glues the crust on; skip it and the crust secedes from the chicken.

i: 600g 80/20 ground beef, loosely rolled into 8 balls, never pressed in advance
Minced onion optional (smashed into the patty)
Sauce: mayo + mustard + pickle brine + paprika; pickles
m: Ripping-hot flat surface. Ball on; smash FLAT with a heavy spatula for 10 firm seconds.
Season; scrape up at 90 seconds with the whole crust attached.
Flip, cheese, 30 seconds. Stack doubles.
Sauced toasted bun. Eat standing over the sink like a person of culture.
p: Smash once, immediately, then never press again: early smash builds crust, late pressing just ejects the juice.

i: 400g sharp cheddar + 150g gruyère or monterey jack, grated (never pre-shredded)
Topping: buttered panko or more cheese
m: Roux 2 min; whisk in milk to a sauce that coats a spoon.
Cheese in off heat, one handful at a time; season boldly.
Fold in pasta; into a buttered dish; top.
Bake 200°C, 20–25 min, to bronze and bubble. Rest 10.
p: Pre-shredded cheese is dusted with anti-caking starch that makes gritty sauce. Grate your own — it's the whole game.

i: Rub: 3 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp paprika, 1 tbsp each salt, pepper, garlic powder; cumin, cayenne
m: Rub the shoulder the night before if you can.
Roast at 135°C, uncovered, 5–7 hours to 95°C internal, until the bone waves goodbye.
Rest 45 min wrapped; shred, folding the crusty bark back in.
Splash with vinegar sauce; pile onto buns under slaw.
p: 95°C internal seems insane until you learn collagen's schedule: 'done' at 70°C, 'pullable' 25 degrees later.

i: 300g flour (soft Southern flour if you can get it)
1 tbsp baking powder, ½ tsp baking soda, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar
m: Toss grated frozen butter through the dry mix.
Add buttermilk; stir until it barely holds.
Fold the shaggy mass over itself 5 times: those are your layers. Pat 2.5cm thick.
Cut straight down, no twisting; bake at 230°C, 12–14 min, touching each other.
p: Twisting the cutter seals the edges shut. Touching biscuits climb each other and rise taller. Physics of breakfast.

i: 240g cornmeal (+ 60g flour, or go 100% corn, Southern-style)
1 tbsp baking powder, ½ tsp soda, 1 tsp salt
80g butter or bacon fat, melted in the skillet
Sugar: 0–2 tbsp, depending which side of the Mason-Dixon you cook for
m: Put the empty cast-iron skillet in a 220°C oven with the fat.
Whisk wet into dry just barely.
Pour batter into the screaming-hot fat: it must sizzle on contact.
Bake 20–22 min; flip out crust-side up.
p: The preheated skillet fries the bottom into a crust; cornbread poured into a cold pan is just corn cake.

i: 2 big bunches collards, ribs stripped, leaves torn
1 smoked ham hock or turkey wing (or smoked paprika + olive oil for veg)
Cider vinegar, hot sauce, pinch sugar, chili flakes
m: Simmer the hock in the stock 30 min head start.
Sweat onion and garlic; add greens in armfuls as they collapse.
Simmer low, partly covered, 45–60 min.
Season the potlikker with vinegar and hot sauce; then guard it. People fight over potlikker.
p: Potlikker, the broth left behind, was once the most nutritious thing on the table. Cornbread exists to be dunked in it.

i: Double crust: 300g flour, 230g cold butter, 1 tsp salt, ice water
120g sugar + brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, lemon
m: Make the crust with visible butter shards; chill 1 h.
Macerate apples with sugar 30 min; drain and REDUCE the juices to a syrup; toss back with starch.
Fill, lid or lattice, vent, wash, sugar.
Bake 220°C for 20 min then 180°C for 40. Cool 3 hours (yes, three).
p: Reducing the drained juice is the anti-soup insurance every soggy pie was missing.

i: 300g flour, 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp salt
250g chocolate, half chips, half chopped bar
m: Brown the butter — nutty, amber, sediment and all.
Whisk with sugars, then eggs and vanilla until glossy.
Fold in dry, then chocolate. REST the dough 1–24 h in the fridge.
Bake 190°C, 11–12 min, until edges set and centers look slightly undone. Flaky salt while warm.
p: Resting hydrates the flour and deepens the toffee notes: a 24-hour cookie tastes like a different recipe.

i: 1kg littleneck clams (or 3 cans + juice, no shame)
m: Steam clams open in a splash of water; chop meat, strain and keep every drop of liquor.
Render bacon; sweat vegetables; flour in for 2 min.
Add clam liquor and potatoes; simmer until tender.
Cream and clams in at the end: clams toughen if boiled. Crackers on top.
p: Clams are done the moment they open. Everything after that is punishment.

i: 600g lamb, hand-chopped or coarsely ground, ~20% fat
1 tbsp Turkish red pepper flakes (pul biber) + 1 tsp Urfa if you have it
1 red pepper, grated and squeezed dry
1 tsp salt, no other seasoning: that is the point
Flat metal skewers, lavash, sumac onions
m: Knead meat, peppers and salt 5 min until tacky and pale: the knead is the binder, there is no egg.
Chill 1 h. Press onto wide flat skewers with wet hands, ridging with your fingers.
Grill over hot coals, turning often, 8–10 min, fat dripping and flaring.
Pull onto lavash so the bread catches the juices; pile with sumac onions and parsley.
p: Adana is licensed by law in its home city: lamb, fat, pepper, salt, nothing else. The knead and the coals do everything a marinade pretends to.

i: Dough: 300g flour, 180ml water, 5g yeast, 1 tsp salt
1 small onion, 1 tomato, ½ red pepper; all minced to a paste
2 tbsp tomato paste, pul biber, parsley
Lemon, more parsley, sumac onions to serve
m: Make a soft dough; rest 1 h. Divide into 6.
Chop the topping almost to a wet paste — it must spread thin, not sit in chunks.
Roll each round paper-thin; smear a thin skim of topping to the very edge.
Bake at max heat on a steel or upside-down tray, 4–6 min. Roll around parsley and a squeeze of lemon; eat like a cigar.
p: Thin is the whole game: the meat should cook in the same minutes as the dough. If your topping is chunky, the dough burns waiting for it.

i: 120ml good olive oil; do not measure with fear
m: Peel aubergines in stripes; fry whole in olive oil until soft and bronzed; slit open like a canoe.
Stew onions slowly in the same oil until sweet; add garlic, tomato, a pinch of sugar.
Stuff the slits generously; nestle in a pan with a splash of water and more oil.
Cover and braise gently 30 min. Cool to room temperature — never serve hot.
p: The name means 'the imam fainted': from the pleasure or the olive oil bill, no one agrees. Room temperature is when the oil, sugar and aubergine finally speak in one voice.

i: Finish: butter bloomed with pul biber, dried mint, lemon wedges
m: Sweat vegetables; stir in tomato paste and cumin.
Add lentils and water; simmer 20 min until everything collapses.
Blend completely smooth: Turkish lentil soup is silk, not rubble.
Sizzle butter with pepper flakes and mint; ribbon it over each bowl. Lemon at the table, always.
p: This soup is on every Turkish table from truck stop to wedding. The lemon is not garnish — the soup is designed unfinished until you squeeze it.

i: 2 green Turkish peppers (or ½ green bell + a hot chili), sliced thin
Pul biber, salt; crusty bread mandatory
m: Soften peppers in the butter and oil 3–4 min.
Add grated tomato; cook down until saucy and no longer watery, 6–8 min.
Crack eggs straight in; stir lazily off and on — big soft curds, not scramble.
Pull off heat while still glossy and loose; dust with pul biber. Serve in the pan.
p: The eternal Turkish argument: onions or no onions. Both camps agree on this: menemen keeps cooking in the pan, so stop one minute before your nerve says so.

i: Dough: 350g flour, 210ml warm water, 7g yeast, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp olive oil
1 onion + 1 pepper + 1 tomato, all finely chopped
Egg yolk + butter for the crust
m: Make a soft dough; rise 1 h. Divide in 3.
Mix meat and vegetables raw — they cook in the oven.
Roll long ovals; spread filling; fold the edges in and pinch the ends into a boat.
Brush rims with yolk; bake at 250°C, 10–12 min; butter the crusts as they land.
p: The boat shape is function: the rim is a handle, the middle is a plate. Slice crosswise and eat the ends first: that is where the crust-to-filling ratio peaks.

i: 200g minced lamb, ½ grated onion, salt, pepper
Sauce: 60g butter, 1 tbsp tomato paste, pul biber
m: Firm dough; rest 30 min. Roll thin; cut 3cm squares.
Dot each with a chickpea-sized bit of filling; pinch corners into tiny parcels.
Boil 8–10 min in salted water.
Plate on garlic yogurt; pour over the sizzling paste-butter; dust mint and sumac.
p: Anatolian grandmothers judge a bride by how small her mantı are; forty on one spoon is the legend. Yours can be big. The yogurt forgives everything.

i: 300g thick yogurt at room temperature, 2 garlic cloves crushed in
1 tsp pul biber + ½ tsp dried mint
m: Whip garlic and salt into the yogurt: room temperature, or it will chill the eggs.
Poach eggs soft, 3 min.
Foam the butter; bloom pepper flakes and mint 10 seconds off heat.
Yogurt in a shallow bowl, eggs on top, red butter over everything.
p: Fifteenth-century Ottoman palace food that costs pennies. The yolk, garlic yogurt and chili butter make a sauce no chef has improved on since.

i: 2 slices stale bread, soaked and squeezed, or 3 tbsp fine bulgur
1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp pul biber, salt, parsley
Grilled peppers, rice or bread, cacık alongside
m: Knead everything 3–4 min until sticky and uniform.
Rest 30 min in the fridge: köfte hold their shape only when cold.
Shape flattened fingers; grill or sear in a cast pan 3 min a side.
Serve with charred green peppers and cool cacık.
p: Squeeze the onion like you mean it. Onion water is the number one cause of köfte that fall apart and steam instead of char.

i: 1 pack filo (fresh if you can find it), ~30 sheets
Syrup: 400g sugar, 300ml water, squeeze of lemon: NO honey in Turkish baklava
Pinch of ground pistachio to crown
m: Butter a tray; lay 12 buttered sheets, then half the nuts, 6 sheets, remaining nuts, 12 sheets.
Cut all the way through into diamonds BEFORE baking.
Bake 170°C, 45–50 min, until deep gold to the bottom.
Boil syrup 10 min; pour COLD syrup over HOT baklava: listen to it crackle. Rest 4 h.
p: Hot pastry, cold syrup, or the reverse, never both hot: that is the difference between crisp layers and a sweet sponge. Gaziantep would also like a word about honey: no.

i: 1 chicken, cut in quarters, slashed to the bone
Jerk paste: 4–6 scotch bonnets, 6 spring onions, thumb of ginger, 6 garlic cloves
2 tbsp allspice berries, thyme, cinnamon, nutmeg
Soy sauce, brown sugar, lime, oil
Pimento wood or a handful of allspice berries for the coals
m: Blitz the paste; massage into the slashes; marinate overnight, no shortcuts here.
Grill over medium coals, lid down, turning every 10 min, ~40 min total.
Throw allspice berries on the coals for the last 10: that smoke is the signature.
Rest, chop through the bone with a cleaver, serve with rice and peas.
p: Jerk is a smoking technique, not a spice mix. Allspice (pimento) wood smoke is the soul; the scotch bonnet is just the sermon.

i: 250g dried kidney beans (the 'peas'), soaked, or 2 cans
4 spring onions, 2 garlic cloves, big sprig thyme
m: Simmer beans in coconut milk and water with aromatics until tender.
Add rice, salt, and float the whole scotch bonnet on top.
Cover tight, lowest heat, 20 min; do not stir, do not peek.
Fish out the bonnet whole; fluff. If it burst, well, say a prayer and taste carefully.
p: The unbroken scotch bonnet perfumes without punishing: fruit-forward heat, no violence. Sunday dinner across Jamaica is measured against this pot.

i: 1 scotch bonnet, 6 spring onions, garlic, ginger, thyme
m: Season meat with curry powder and aromatics; marinate overnight.
'Burn the curry': fry another spoon of curry powder in oil until it darkens and smells toasty.
Brown meat in that; add water to barely cover; simmer 2–2.5 h until sliding off the bone.
Potatoes in for the last 30 — they thicken the gravy as they fray at the edges.
p: Burning the curry, blooming it in hot oil until it deepens, is the step that separates curry goat from stew with curry powder in it.

i: 2 onions, 2 bell peppers, sliced; 6 garlic cloves
2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp oregano, 2 bay leaves
Pimento-stuffed olives + capers; white rice and black beans to serve
m: Simmer flank with bay and half an onion until it surrenders, ~2 h. Shred into rags; keep the broth.
Sofrito: slow-fry onions, peppers, garlic; add cumin and oregano.
Wine, tomatoes, a ladle of broth; simmer 15 min.
Fold in the shredded beef and olives; simmer until the 'old clothes' soak up the sauce.
p: The name means 'old rags': the beef must be shredded along the grain into threads, never cubed. The olives are Cuba's little salt-bombs; do not skip them.

i: 150g chicharrón (crisp pork skin) or crispy bacon
6 garlic cloves, mashed with olive oil and salt
Chicken broth or garlic-butter shrimp to serve over
m: Peel plantains; slice thick; fry at 170°C until tender and gold, not crisp.
In a pilón (mortar), smash hot plantains with the garlic paste.
Fold in chicharrón as you pound: crunch through the mash.
Pack into a bowl, unmold, moat with hot broth or crown with shrimp.
p: Mofongo waits for no one: plantains seize as they cool. Pound hot, serve hotter, and the broth on the side is there to loosen every bite.

i: Pastry: 350g flour, 1 tbsp turmeric + curry powder, 200g cold butter/suet, ice water
Scotch bonnet, spring onion, garlic, thyme, allspice
m: Make the golden pastry; rest 1 h: turmeric is for the famous yellow.
Cook the filling; add crumbs and stock so it sets soft and spoonable, not dry.
Roll, cut circles, fill, fold, crimp with a fork.
Bake 200°C, 25–30 min.
p: The filling must be almost porridge-soft going in: it firms as it bakes. A dry patty filling is a crime the crust cannot pardon.

i: 300g salt cod, soaked overnight, water changed twice
1 can ackee, drained gently (fresh if you are lucky and careful)
Scotch bonnet to taste, black pepper
Fried dumplings or boiled green banana alongside
m: Boil soaked cod 15 min; flake, discarding skin and bone.
Sauté onion, thyme, bonnet, tomato in a generous pan.
Fold in the fish; heat through.
Add ackee last; fold ONCE or twice: it crumbles like scrambled eggs if bullied.
p: Jamaica's national dish. Ackee is buttery and fragile: treat it like a soft scramble, folding, never stirring, and it rewards you.

i: Bara: 250g flour, 1 tsp yeast, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp ground cumin, water
Channa: 2 cans chickpeas, 2 tbsp curry powder, garlic, onion
m: Soft, slack dough; rise 1 h.
Curry the chickpeas until tender and saucy, crushing a few to thicken.
With oiled hands, stretch dough into thin rounds; fry seconds a side: they should puff and stay soft.
Two bara, channa between, sauces on top. Eat standing up, leaning forward.
p: The national street breakfast of Trinidad. 'Slight pepper' is the standard order, and the lean-forward stance is structural, not optional.

i: 3 green plantains, green as a traffic light, no yellow
Garlic dipping sauce: mashed garlic, oil, lime (mojo)
m: Peel (score the skin lengthwise, lever it off); slice 2.5cm rounds.
First fry: 160°C until tender and pale gold, 3–4 min. Drain.
Smash each flat with a cup bottom or tostonera.
Second fry: 190°C until shatter-crisp. Salt in the air the second they land.
p: The double fry is non-negotiable: first fry cooks, smash creates surface, second fry crisps. Dip in salted garlic water before round two for the Puerto Rican abuela upgrade.

i: 2 parts sugar syrup or grenadine ('two of sweet')
3 parts dark Caribbean rum ('three of strong')
4 parts fruit juice, orange + pineapple ('four of weak')
m: Stir sour, sweet, strong, weak in a jug.
Add a good dash of Angostura.
Chill properly — punch is best after an hour making friends with itself.
Serve over ice; grate nutmeg on top.
p: The recipe is a 300-year-old rhyme: one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong, four of weak. Say it once and you will never need to look it up again.

i: 6 tomatoes + 2 red bell peppers + 1 scotch bonnet + 1 onion, blended
2 tsp curry powder, thyme, bay, stock cubes (this is tradition, not shame)
m: Reduce the blended base in oil with tomato paste until it darkens and the oil rises: 20 min, do not rush the fry.
Season hard: curry powder, thyme, bay, stock.
Stir in rice; add water just level with the rice; cover with foil then lid.
Lowest heat 30 min. Let the bottom catch a little: that smoky base note is the point.
p: The slightly burnt bottom layer is prized from Lagos to Accra: party jollof tastes of smoke on purpose. As for Ghana vs Nigeria: I cook both and stay out of the war.

i: Blended pepper mix: tomato, red bell, scotch bonnet, onion
2 big handfuls spinach or bitterleaf; crayfish powder, stock
m: Simmer meats seasoned until tender; keep the stock.
Fry pepper mix in palm oil; mix egusi with a little water into a paste.
Add egusi in clumps; let them set 10 min before breaking into curds.
Loosen with stock, return meat, wilt in the greens. Serve with pounded yam or fufu.
p: Let the egusi lumps steam-set before stirring: those curds are the texture people fight over. Stir too soon and you get porridge, not soup.

i: 500g beef sirloin, sliced thin against the grain
Yaji: 4 tbsp ground roasted peanuts (oil pressed out), 1 tbsp ginger, 1 tbsp paprika
1 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 stock cube, crushed
Raw onion rings, tomato, extra yaji to serve
m: Make yaji: peanuts must be roasted, ground, and squeezed in paper until almost dry.
Oil the beef; press yaji into every face; thread ribbons on skewers; rest 30 min.
Grill hot and fast, 3 min a side, brushing with oil.
Serve wrapped in paper with raw onion and a dusting of fresh yaji.
p: Nigerian street mastery: the peanut must be dry or the crust turns to paste on the grill. Suya without extra yaji on the side is just kebab.

i: Juice of 4 limes + 4 tbsp Dijon mustard
Oil, bay, green olives, rice to serve
m: Marinate chicken in lime, mustard, garlic and a third of the onions, overnight.
Char the chicken hard on a grill or in a pan; set aside.
Stew ALL the onions in oil, low and slow, 30 min, until melting and sweet.
Add marinade, bonnet and chicken; simmer 30 min. Olives at the end.
p: Senegal's gift: the onions are the sauce — six onions collapse into something between confit and gravy, sharpened by lime and mustard. Do not brown them; melt them.

i: 800g beef or lamb chunks (or sweet potato + cabbage for veg)
Carrots, sweet potato, cabbage wedges; rice to serve
m: Brown meat; fry onion, garlic, tomato paste.
Add tomatoes and water; simmer meat 45 min.
Whisk peanut butter with hot broth; stir in; add vegetables.
Simmer uncovered 30 min until the oil rises to the top and the sauce clings.
p: When the peanut oil breaks and beads on the surface, the mafe is done: that sheen is West Africa's version of a reduced French sauce.

i: 500g cassava (or plantain + cassava mix; or cassava flour for the fast road)
Pinch of salt (controversial; many say none)
A strong wooden spoon and stronger forearms
m: Boil peeled cassava until completely soft.
Pound (or beat in a stand mixer with paddle, modern kitchen truce) adding splashes of hot water.
Work until stretchy, smooth and lump-free: it should slump slowly, not hold peaks.
Shape into smooth mounds with wet hands. Serve with egusi or mafe.
p: Fufu is cutlery: pinch, roll, dent, scoop, swallow. Chewing is technically allowed but culturally discouraged.

i: 4 ripe plantains, yellow with black spots
1 tsp cayenne, ½ tsp nutmeg, pinch of cloves
Salt, splash of water to make a paste
Oil for frying; roasted peanuts to serve
m: Cube plantains.
Toss in the ginger-spice paste; sit 10 min.
Fry at 180°C until mahogany at the edges.
Drain, salt, scatter peanuts. Best eaten from paper at dusk, Accra-style.
p: Ripe plantain caramelizes where green plantain crisps — kelewele is candy-edged and fluffy inside, the opposite argument to tostones, and both are right.

i: 4 thick fish steaks (grouper/snapper); stuffing: parsley, garlic, chili pounded to a paste (rof)
4 tbsp tomato paste, 1 onion, dried fish or shrimp (optional funk)
Vegetables: cassava, carrot, cabbage, aubergine, okra
m: Slit fish; pack with rof paste.
Fry tomato paste and onion in oil; add water, vegetables, fish; simmer: fish out at 15 min, veg when tender.
Cook rice IN that red broth until it drinks it all.
Platter: red rice, fish, vegetables arranged like a market stall; scrape the crust from the pot for the elders.
p: Senegal's national dish and jollof's acknowledged ancestor. The crusty rice at the pot's bottom (xoon) is served with ceremony; burn it a little on purpose.

i: 300g black-eyed peas, soaked and SKINNED (rub in water, skins float off)
1 red bell pepper, ½ onion, 1 scotch bonnet
3 tbsp oil or palm oil, stock cube, salt
Optional: boiled egg quarters, flaked fish
Banana leaves, ramekins or foil cups
m: Blend skinned peas with pepper, onion and minimal water: thick as pancake batter.
Whisk in oil and seasoning until airy.
Pour into leaves or cups; tuck in egg if using.
Steam 45–50 min until set like firm custard.
p: Skinning the beans is the tedious step everyone tries to skip and always regrets: skins make it coarse and bitter. Rub, float, discard, thank yourself.

i: 1 tbsp yeast, 80g sugar, ½ tsp salt
Oil for deep frying; sugar to dust
m: Whisk everything into a thick, stretchy batter; rise 1 h until bubbly.
Heat oil to 170°C.
Scoop with your hand: squeeze batter through your fist and thumb into balls (or use two spoons, coward's route).
Fry, rolling, until deep gold; dust with sugar.
p: The hand-squeeze drop is the true technique and worth learning: perfectly round puff puff marks you as someone who was taught, not someone who watched a video.

i: 600g mixed pork: shoulder, ribs, smoked sausage, bacon (traditionally ears and trotters too)
Orange slices, white rice, collard ribbons, farofa
m: Simmer beans with bay; separately brown the meats in stages.
Unite everything; simmer 2–3 h, lazy bubbles, until the broth turns black velvet.
Mash a ladle of beans against the pot wall to thicken.
Serve with rice, quick-fried collards, farofa and orange slices: the orange is digestive strategy, not decoration.
p: Brazil's Saturday ritual: feijoada is eaten at noon because nobody is expected to function afterward. The orange cuts the richness; trust two centuries of precedent.

i: 250g sour tapioca starch (polvilho azedo, the sour matters)
